findings.title: 4. Store Test Findings Once
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/test-attempt-007.json`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** The same finding is duplicated in `blockingFindings` and `findings`, with repeated IDs, fingerprint, title, rationale, and issue/body text.  
**Suggestion:** Store one canonical `findings` array with severity/kind fields, then derive `blockingFindings` as references, counts, or a rendered view.

findings.title: 1. Deduplicate Work Unit Identity Metadata
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/11401db1d0226f1231be2ae2.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** The same execution identity fields are stored both at the top level and under `identity`: `unitId`, `targetFiles`, `inputHash`, `providerIdentity`, `promptVersion`, and `schemaVersion`. This creates two sources of truth inside the artifact.  
**Suggestion:** Keep identity metadata in one canonical location. For example, retain immutable execution identity under `identity` and remove the duplicated top-level copies, leaving only run-result fields such as `status`, `attemptCount`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt`, and `success`.

findings.title: 2. Avoid Persisting Raw And Parsed Proposal Copies
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/2802ea34b3003a0b446168d0.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `rawResponse` stores the full Markdown proposal output, while `success.proposals` stores parsed versions of the same proposals. This duplicates the largest content in the artifact and increases drift/debug ambiguity.  
**Suggestion:** Make `success.proposals` the canonical successful result. Store only a compact raw-response audit such as a digest, provider length, and proposal count, or retain full raw output only for failed parses.

findings.title: 3. Add An Explicit Raw Output Size Bound
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/427dfbd203456f4fae825b67.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `rawResponse` appears to persist provider output without an explicit size cap. That conflicts with the `bounded-resource-usage` guardrail because provider-generated bulk text can grow without a clear persisted-data bound.  
**Suggestion:** Enforce a maximum stored `rawResponse` length, truncating with a marker and digest, or omit raw output after successful parsing.

findings.title: 5. Generate Markdown From Canonical JSON
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/test-attempt-008.md`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** The Markdown file duplicates content already present in `test-attempt-008.json`, including verdict, coverage artifact, target, improvement, and rationale.  
**Suggestion:** Treat the JSON file as canonical and generate the Markdown view on demand, or reduce the Markdown artifact to a compact pointer/index if both files must exist.

findings.title: 5. Generate Markdown From Canonical JSON
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/test-review.md`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** The Markdown file duplicates content already present in `test-attempt-008.json`, including verdict, coverage artifact, target, improvement, and rationale.  
**Suggestion:** Treat the JSON file as canonical and generate the Markdown view on demand, or reduce the Markdown artifact to a compact pointer/index if both files must exist.

findings.title: 5. Bound retained raw provider output
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/562c706852c82bb0fcee42e9.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** `rawResponse` stores full provider output inline with no visible size limit or truncation metadata. Repeated loop chunks can accumulate unbounded text, conflicting with the bounded-resource-usage guardrail.
**Suggestion:** Add a maximum persisted character count for `rawResponse`, include truncation metadata such as `rawResponseTruncated`, or store only structured proposals plus a digest of the raw response.

findings.title: 3. Avoid storing proposals twice
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/591b4feebb7073ebc2e7b66d.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** The proposal text is stored in full in `rawResponse` and again inside `success.proposals[].body`, with duplicated `file` and `requirementId` metadata. This bloats generated artifacts and can drift.
**Suggestion:** Treat `success.proposals` as canonical structured data, and replace `rawResponse` with a hash, bounded diagnostic excerpt, or omit it after successful parsing.

findings.title: 1. Keep parsed proposals consistent with raw output
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/c43a47f76d207c075c9f3648.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** `rawResponse` contains seven proposals, but `success.proposals` is an empty array. This creates two conflicting representations of the same review result and makes downstream tooling likely to treat a successful proposal run as having no proposals.
**Suggestion:** Populate `success.proposals` from `rawResponse`, or mark the unit as a parse failure with explicit error metadata if parsing failed.

findings.title: 2. Collapse duplicated work-unit metadata
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/75f4871091a34c2fc78b9a8b.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** `phase`, `kind`, `unitId`, `targetFiles`, `inputHash`, `providerIdentity`, `promptVersion`, and `schemaVersion` are stored both at the top level and under `identity`. This repeats the same state and creates drift risk.
**Suggestion:** Keep immutable identity fields under `identity` only, and reserve top-level fields for execution state like `status`, `attemptCount`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt`, and `success`.

findings.title: 4. Remove display numbering from stored titles
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/8dd631de9065ac75b1dfdc57.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** `success.proposals[].title` includes ordinal prefixes like `1.` and `2.` even though array order already captures sequencing. This mixes presentation formatting into stored data.
**Suggestion:** Store clean titles without numbering and add numbering only when rendering Markdown output.

findings.title: 2. Deduplicate target file lists
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/d7e860f04f301bf9cac6a177.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** The same `targetFiles` array is stored twice: once under `identity.targetFiles` and again at top level. This duplicates a large path list and creates drift risk. The same pattern appears in the other new work-unit JSON files.  
**Suggestion:** Make one location canonical. Prefer keeping `identity.targetFiles` if it is part of the stable identity hash, and have readers derive the top-level view when needed.

findings.title: 3. Avoid storing proposals twice
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/d85e17476af5711ba3ad8791.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** Each proposal is stored once as formatted Markdown inside `rawResponse` and again as structured entries under `success.proposals`. This creates two sources of truth for title, file, requirement, issue, and suggestion content.  
**Suggestion:** Store structured proposals as canonical data and render Markdown on demand, or store only `rawResponse` plus parsing metadata if raw provider output must be preserved.

findings.title: 1. Remove invalid cross-scope proposal payloads
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/f11405f01831676c001ddd2a.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** Several embedded proposals in `rawResponse` and `success.proposals` name files that are not part of the displayed diff, violating the mandatory touched-file scope contract for this review artifact.  
**Suggestion:** Regenerate this work-unit output so every embedded proposal targets only files present in the current diff, or drop out-of-scope proposals before persisting `rawResponse` and `success.proposals`.

findings.title: 4. Normalize duplicated identity fields
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/f11405f01831676c001ddd2a.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** Fields such as `unitId`, `inputHash`, `providerIdentity`, `promptVersion`, and `schemaVersion` are repeated both inside `identity` and at the top level. This makes the schema noisier and risks inconsistent updates.  
**Suggestion:** Keep stable identity fields only under `identity`, and reserve top-level fields for execution state such as `status`, `attemptCount`, `startedAt`, and `finishedAt`.

findings.title: 5. Compact repeated scenario evidence
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/scenario-validity-result.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** Every requirement entry repeats the same command, test file, and raw output line range. This is duplicate data and makes later updates easy to desynchronize.  
**Suggestion:** Move shared evidence fields to a top-level `evidence` object and let each summary entry contain only requirement id, classification, test name, and any requirement-specific line range.

findings.title: 6. Bound raw output references
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/scenario-validity-result.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** Each evidence entry points to raw output lines `1..6246`, effectively tying every requirement to a large unbounded log span. This conflicts with the bounded-resource-usage guardrail.  
**Suggestion:** Store bounded per-test evidence windows, such as the exact subtest diagnostic line range plus a capped context size, and add an explicit maximum retained raw-output length.

findings.title: 7. Remove empty Markdown sections
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/spec.md`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `Clarifications (Q&A)` contains empty `Q`/`A` bullets and `Open Questions` contains only an empty checkbox. These are dead generated placeholders that add noise without meaning.  
**Suggestion:** Omit empty sections from the Markdown renderer, or render them as a compact `None` only when the section is required by downstream tooling.

findings.title: 8. Align task status with completed requirements
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/spec.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** All requirements are marked `done`, but tasks `T-1`, `T-2`, and `T-3` remain `pending`. This inconsistent state makes the artifact harder to reason about and can confuse automation that reads task status.  
**Suggestion:** Update task statuses to match the completed requirement state, or add a distinct lifecycle field if tasks intentionally track a different phase than requirements.

findings.title: 1. Deduplicate repeated guardrail findings
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/task-impl-gate-source.json`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** The same `no-overengineering` finding is represented twice under `evaluations` and again twice under top-level `observations`, with near-identical `reason`, `observed`, `rationale`, and duplicated fingerprints. This makes the artifact noisy and increases the chance that downstream consumers count one issue multiple times.  
**Suggestion:** Collapse these into one canonical finding with multiple locations, or keep one `evaluations` entry and derive `observations` from it instead of storing duplicated copies. If the schema requires both sections, ensure each logical finding has one stable id and one shared source of truth for the message text.

findings.title: 1. Bound and clean up temporary test projects
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/tests/required-hook-failure-policy.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** Several tests create temp directories with `fs.mkdtempSync(...)` and never remove them. This leaks filesystem resources across repeated test runs.  
**Suggestion:** Use the existing `createTmpDir` / `removeTmpDir` pattern or register `t.after(() => removeTmpDir(projectRoot))` for every temp project.

findings.title: 2. Extract repeated hook snapshot fixtures
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/tests/required-hook-failure-policy.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** Snapshot objects for `FixtureHook`, finalize hooks, and advisory/required cases are repeated many times with only small field differences.  
**Suggestion:** Add helpers such as `prepareHookSnapshot({ policy, command, hook, module, className })` and `finalizeHookSnapshot(...)` to reduce duplication and make policy differences easier to audit.

findings.title: 3. Extract repeated finalize hook file setup
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/tests/required-hook-failure-policy.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** The finalize hook module creation is duplicated in multiple tests with nearly identical class bodies and snapshot setup.  
**Suggestion:** Add a helper like `writeFinalizeHook(projectRoot, { className, body })` and reuse it for branch and worktree finalize cases.

findings.title: 4. Reuse plugin lifecycle composition logic
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** `composeFinalizePluginLifecycle` duplicates lifecycle-composition behavior already introduced in `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`, increasing the chance that prepare and finalize diverge later.  
**Suggestion:** Export a small lifecycle composition helper from `plugin-registry.js` or return a shared lifecycle result shape from `runFlowCommandHooks`, then reuse it in finalize-cleanup.

findings.title: 5. Simplify finalize pre/post hook orchestration
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** Spec-only and teardown paths each manually build plugin context, run pre hooks, run post hooks, check required failures, and attach lifecycle data.  
**Suggestion:** Extract a helper such as `runFinalizePluginLifecycleAround(ctx, state, pluginContext, main)` to centralize pre/post handling and required-failure conversion.

findings.title: 6. Rename `writeFlowState` after behavior expansion
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** `writeFlowState(extra, writePrepareFiles)` now runs the plugin lifecycle, writes spec files, creates flow state, and publishes repair baseline. The name understates its side effects.  
**Suggestion:** Rename it to something like `runPrepareLifecycleAndPersistFlow` or split plugin lifecycle orchestration from persistence.

findings.title: 7. Remove redundant catch block
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** The `try { ... } catch (error) { throw error; }` inside `writeFlowState` adds no behavior.  
**Suggestion:** Remove the redundant catch and let errors propagate naturally.

findings.title: 8. Bound raw scenario-validity artifact size
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/tests/.raw/scenario-validity.log`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** The raw log embeds thousands of lines of source text from an assertion failure, creating an oversized generated artifact. This also conflicts with the bounded-resource-usage guardrail.  
**Suggestion:** Regenerate the scenario-validity artifact with bounded failure excerpts, or adjust the failing assertion/reporting path so raw logs capture concise evidence rather than full file contents.

findings.title: 1. Extract hook metadata fixture helper
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/finalize-cleanup-transaction-v2.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** Hook metadata is duplicated between the dynamically written plugin class and `fixture.state.plugins.flowCommandHooks`, including `command`, `hook`, and `failurePolicy`. This makes tests brittle if required hook metadata changes again.  
**Suggestion:** Add a small local helper for building the hook registration metadata, or constants per test for `command`, `hook`, and `failurePolicy`, then reuse them in both the hook source and fixture state.

findings.title: 2. Extract plugin installation setup
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/finalize-cleanup-transaction-v2.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The test now writes the same plugin config and hook source into both the main root and worktree, then stages and commits the worktree copy inline. This setup is fairly specific and obscures the behavior under test.  
**Suggestion:** Extract this into a helper such as `installFinalizeHookPluginInRootAndWorktree(...)` that writes config, writes hook source, creates directories, and commits the worktree runtime files.

findings.title: 3. Extract fake flow manager transition application
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/set-step-impl-repair.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The fake `flowManager.updateStepStatus` implementation repeats the same transition application logic in multiple tests: assert intent, apply status changes, then apply intent.  
**Suggestion:** Add a helper like `createFlowManagerStub(state, { transitions })` or `applyTransitionChanges(state, transition)` to keep the tests focused on scenario setup and assertions.

findings.title: 4. Clarify optional fixture cleanup intent
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/set-step-impl-repair.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R4  
**Issue:** `fs.rmSync(..., { force: true })` makes missing `impl-review.json` and `impl-triage.json` silently acceptable, but the test does not explain whether those files are intentionally optional in this fixture.  
**Suggestion:** Rename this setup block through a helper such as `removeOptionalImplArtifacts(specDir)` or add a short comment explaining that these files may not exist depending on fixture evolution.

findings.title: 1. Normalize Finding Identity Across Review Artifacts
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/test-attempt-001.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** Multiple artifact families repeat the same identity inconsistency: `findingId` and `fingerprint` are often identical, while some distinct findings share the same identifier across locations or requirements. This appears in gate sources, review evidence, review history, and flow findings, making deduplication and repair targeting ambiguous.
**Suggestion:** Define one canonical finding identity contract shared by gate, evidence, history, and flow artifacts. Use one primary ID field, and include requirement/location/content inputs when generating IDs for independently actionable findings.

findings.title: 2. Use One Canonical Finding Schema
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/impl-attempt-006.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** Several JSON artifacts store full finding payloads twice under paired collections such as `blockingFindings` and `findings`, with inconsistent field names like `issue` vs `body`, `kind` vs `severity`, and `failureMode` vs `category`.
**Suggestion:** Persist findings once in a shared canonical schema, then derive grouped views such as blocking/advisory findings by ID, severity, or category during rendering.

findings.title: 3. Generate Markdown Review Artifacts From JSON
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/test-attempt-003.md`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** Review-history Markdown files duplicate adjacent JSON artifacts across impl, spec, and test attempts. This creates two sources of truth for verdicts, findings, files, requirements, issues, suggestions, and rationales.
**Suggestion:** Treat JSON as the canonical persisted artifact and generate Markdown on demand, or reduce Markdown files to compact summaries that reference the JSON artifact.

findings.title: 4. Consolidate Work-Unit Identity Metadata
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/d7e860f04f301bf9cac6a177.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** Work-unit JSON files repeatedly store identity fields both at the top level and under `identity`, including `unitId`, `targetFiles`, `inputHash`, `providerIdentity`, `promptVersion`, and `schemaVersion`.
**Suggestion:** Keep immutable identity metadata only under `identity`, and reserve top-level fields for execution state such as `status`, `attemptCount`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt`, and `success`.

findings.title: 5. Avoid Persisting Raw And Parsed Provider Output Together
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-history/work-units/impl-review/591b4feebb7073ebc2e7b66d.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** Multiple work-unit artifacts store full Markdown provider output in `rawResponse` and parsed proposal data in `success.proposals`, duplicating large proposal bodies and creating parse-state drift risk.
**Suggestion:** Make `success.proposals` canonical after successful parsing. Store only a digest, bounded excerpt, length, and proposal count for raw output, retaining full raw text only for parse failures.

findings.title: 6. Add A Shared Retention Policy For Generated History
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/flow.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** Several generated artifact families appear append-only or unbounded: flow metrics/history arrays, review evidence, review history attempts, work-unit raw output, repair fingerprints, issue logs, and raw scenario-validity logs.
**Suggestion:** Introduce a shared retention policy for generated workflow artifacts, such as latest N entries per phase plus `omittedCount`, summaries, digests, and explicit truncation metadata.

findings.title: 7. Standardize Review Artifact Formatting
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/review-evidence/def3a5a0e158ad9dca2d9d95a9f1cef30394d77a082c2c6eb29c08b05862cf02.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** Review evidence JSON files are single-line while related review-history JSON files are pretty-printed, and some Markdown artifacts lack final newlines. The formatting policy differs across generated artifacts in the same workflow.
**Suggestion:** Use one generator-level formatting convention for all review artifacts, for example stable pretty-printed JSON with trailing newline and Markdown files with trailing newline.

findings.title: 8. Extract Shared Empty Artifact Builders
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/draft-review-coverage.json`
**Requirement:** R3
**Issue:** Empty PASS, triage, repair, coverage, and question artifacts repeat nearly identical structures across files, differing only by phase, source pointer, timestamp, and summary text.
**Suggestion:** Generate empty review and repair artifacts from shared builders or schemas parameterized by phase, source field, and summary text.

findings.title: 9. Reuse Plugin Lifecycle Composition Across Prepare And Finalize
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`
**Requirement:** R7
**Issue:** Prepare and finalize code paths appear to introduce separate plugin lifecycle composition logic, with finalize-specific helpers duplicating behavior already present in plugin registry or prepare orchestration.
**Suggestion:** Extract a shared lifecycle composition/orchestration helper used by both prepare and finalize paths, with command-specific context supplied as parameters.

findings.title: 10. Align Flow Status Artifacts With Spec Completion State
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/spec.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** Cross-file workflow state is inconsistent: requirements are marked `done`, tasks remain `pending`, and `flow.json` still marks `impl-review` as `in_progress` even though later review, gate, and regression artifacts exist.
**Suggestion:** Regenerate or normalize workflow state so requirement, task, step, and attempt artifacts use one lifecycle model and agree on terminal statuses.

nonBlockingImprovements.title: 4. Remove Redundant Empty Repair Artifact When No Work Exists
nonBlockingImprovements.issue:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/draft-coverage-repair.json`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The file records only “No draft triage items to repair” with an empty `items` array. If this artifact is generated every time there is no repair work, it adds repository churn without carrying actionable state.  
**Suggestion:** Skip generating this file when `items` is empty, or replace it with a single shared status field in the preceding triage artifact if consumers need to know that repair was intentionally unnecessary.

**Suggestion:** Collapse identical findings into one entry per fingerprint and store all affected locators in a bounded array, e.g. `locations: [...]`, or ensure each repeated observation has a distinct fingerprint if it represents a separate actionable finding.

**Suggestion:** Keep the canonical finding payload in one section and let the other section reference it by `findingId`/`fingerprint`, or reduce `observations` to location-level details while `evaluations` owns the finding summary.

**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The artifact uses both `guardrail_id` and `guardrailId` for the same concept. This naming inconsistency increases parser complexity and invites drift.  
**Suggestion:** Use one field name consistently throughout the artifact. Since other camelCase fields exist (`findingId`, `requirementId`, `reportedAt`), prefer `guardrailId` unless an external schema explicitly requires `guardrail_id`.

**Suggestion:** Narrow this to fixtures and helpers that directly construct `plugins.flowCommandHooks` snapshots for the affected lifecycle tests, or state a concrete discovery rule such as “all references found by searching for `flowCommandHooks` in touched spec/test fixtures.”

**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** The issue number is stored twice as `issue` and `result.issueNumber`, which creates unnecessary duplication and a risk of inconsistency.

nonBlockingImprovements.title: 2. Reconcile Conflicting Gate And Review Results
nonBlockingImprovements.issue:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/spec-review.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `spec-review.json` reports `verdict: "PASS"` with zero findings, while `spec-gate-source.json` in the same change set reports `result: "fail"` with a blocking violation. These artifacts appear inconsistent.

**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The file records only “No draft triage items to repair” with an empty `items` array. If this artifact is generated every time there is no repair work, it adds repository churn without carrying actionable state.  
**Suggestion:** Skip generating this file when `items` is empty, or replace it with a single shared status field in the preceding triage artifact if consumers need to know that repair was intentionally unnecessary.

findings.title: 1. Deduplicate Repeated Guardrail Findings
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/draft-gate-source.json`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The same `prioritize-requirements` failure appears multiple times with identical `findingId`, `fingerprint`, `reason`, `rationale`, and metadata, differing only by locator. This makes the gate source noisy and harder to review.  
**Suggestion:** Collapse identical findings into one entry per fingerprint and store all affected locators in a bounded array, e.g. `locations: [...]`, or ensure each repeated observation has a distinct fingerprint if it represents a separate actionable finding.

findings.title: 2. Avoid Duplicating Full Finding Data Across Sections
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/draft-gate-source.json`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** `evaluations` and `observations` repeat much of the same information, including guardrail IDs, rationale, disposition, timestamps, and fingerprints. This creates two sources of truth inside the same artifact.  
**Suggestion:** Keep the canonical finding payload in one section and let the other section reference it by `findingId`/`fingerprint`, or reduce `observations` to location-level details while `evaluations` owns the finding summary.

findings.title: 3. Normalize Guardrail Field Naming
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/draft-gate-source.json`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The artifact uses both `guardrail_id` and `guardrailId` for the same concept. This naming inconsistency increases parser complexity and invites drift.  
**Suggestion:** Use one field name consistently throughout the artifact. Since other camelCase fields exist (`findingId`, `requirementId`, `reportedAt`), prefer `guardrailId` unless an external schema explicitly requires `guardrail_id`.

findings.title: 1. Remove duplicated bilingual requirement body
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/issue.md`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** The Japanese `<details>` section repeats the full Summary, Decision, Requirements, Scope, Out of Scope, Acceptance Criteria, and Evidence content already stated in English. This creates two authoritative copies that can drift during later edits.  
**Suggestion:** Keep one canonical requirements body and replace the Japanese section with a short localized summary or remove it if bilingual duplication is not required.

findings.title: 2. Consolidate repeated failure matrix wording
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/draft.json`  
**Requirement:** R3  
**Issue:** The required/advisory failure matrix is repeated across `analysis.validation`, `scopeVerification.in`, and `impactOnExisting` with slightly different phrasing. This makes future changes to covered failure modes error-prone.  
**Suggestion:** Define the lifecycle matrix once in a dedicated field, then reference it from validation/scope/impact text instead of restating the full list each time.

findings.title: 3. Add explicit bounded wording for fixture/test-helper updates
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/issue.md`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** The scope says to update “the fixtures / test helpers that build it” without a bound or selection rule. Under the bounded-resource-usage guardrail, bulk updates should have an explicit limit or deterministic scope.  
**Suggestion:** Narrow this to fixtures and helpers that directly construct `plugins.flowCommandHooks` snapshots for the affected lifecycle tests, or state a concrete discovery rule such as “all references found by searching for `flowCommandHooks` in touched spec/test fixtures.”

findings.title: 1. Remove Redundant Issue Number Field
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/plugin-artifacts/workflow/prepare.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** The issue number is stored twice as `issue` and `result.issueNumber`, which creates unnecessary duplication and a risk of inconsistency.  
**Suggestion:** Keep a single source of truth. Prefer either the top-level `issue` field or `result.issueNumber`, but not both.

findings.title: 2. Reconcile Conflicting Gate And Review Results
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/spec-review.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `spec-review.json` reports `verdict: "PASS"` with zero findings, while `spec-gate-source.json` in the same change set reports `result: "fail"` with a blocking violation. These artifacts appear inconsistent.  
**Suggestion:** Regenerate or update `spec-review.json` so its verdict and finding counts reflect the blocking gate failure, or remove the stale artifact if it should not be committed.

findings.title: 1. Add Explicit Bounds To Snapshot Comparisons
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/spec.json`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** The test strategy requires byte-for-byte snapshots of flow state, issue-log, spec/draft files, plugin artifact directories, and Git/worktree state, but it does not define any upper bound for directory traversal, file count, file size, or total bytes. This violates `bounded-resource-usage` for bulk data loading.  
**Suggestion:** Add explicit caps to the relevant acceptance criteria or test strategy, such as maximum artifact directory depth, maximum file count, maximum per-file bytes, and maximum total snapshot bytes. Also define the expected failure behavior when those caps are exceeded.

findings.title: 2. Remove Empty Placeholder Sections
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/spec.md`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `## Clarifications (Q&A)` contains empty `Q:` / `A:` bullets, and `## Open Questions` contains only `- [ ]`. These are dead placeholder content and make the spec look less finalized than the `PASS` review suggests.  
**Suggestion:** Remove the empty placeholder entries, or render these sections as `None` / `No open questions` consistently.

findings.title: 3. Consolidate Repeated Lifecycle Atomicity Text
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/spec.md`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** The same prepare/finalize-cleanup atomicity surfaces are repeated in the Goal, Scope, Design Principles, Overview, R6, AC5, AC6, and T-3. This increases maintenance risk if the protected surface list changes.  
**Suggestion:** Define a single named list of protected prepare and finalize-cleanup surfaces, then reference that list from requirements, acceptance criteria, and task descriptions.

findings.title: 1. Deduplicate Repeated Guardrail Findings
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/task-impl-gate-source.json`  
**Requirement:** R2  
**Issue:** The same two `no-overengineering` findings are repeated in both `evaluations[]` and top-level `observations[]`, with largely identical rationale text and metadata. This makes the artifact harder to review and increases the chance of inconsistent future updates.  
**Suggestion:** Store the canonical finding data once and have the other section reference it by `findingId`/`fingerprint`, or remove one redundant representation if consumers do not require both.

findings.title: 2. Use Concrete Requirement IDs In Gate Findings
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/task-impl-gate-source.json`  
**Requirement:** R2  
**Issue:** Each finding has `"requirementId": null` while the review contract requires findings to map to known requirement IDs. That weakens traceability from implementation gate failures back to the spec contract.  
**Suggestion:** Populate `requirementId` with the relevant requirement, likely `R2` for typed hook outcome handling or `R6` if the finding is specifically about finalize-cleanup pre-hook stop behavior.

findings.title: 3. Avoid Duplicated Long Rationale Text
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/task-impl-gate-source.json`  
**Requirement:** R2  
**Issue:** `reason`, `observed`, and `rationale` repeat the same long text within each finding. This is noisy and makes the generated JSON unnecessarily large.  
**Suggestion:** Keep the detailed text in one canonical field, such as `rationale`, and make `reason` a short summary or derive it when rendering human-readable output.

findings.title: 1. Remove Duplicated Advisory Text
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/test-review.json`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** The advisory finding stores the same sentence in both `rationale` and `whyNonBlocking`, which creates duplicate maintenance surface and makes the fields less semantically distinct.
**Suggestion:** Keep `rationale` focused on why the finding exists, and reserve `whyNonBlocking` for why it does not block. For example, make `rationale` describe the artifact-write ambiguity, while `whyNonBlocking` keeps the current coverage justification.

findings.title: 1. Extract Snapshot Fixture Builders
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/tests/required-hook-failure-policy.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** Hook snapshot objects are repeated throughout the test file with mostly identical fields, which makes policy/module/class changes noisy and easy to miss.  
**Suggestion:** Add helpers such as `prepareHookSnapshot(overrides = {})` and `finalizeHookSnapshot(overrides = {})`, then use overrides for `failurePolicy`, `module`, `className`, `command`, and `hook`.

findings.title: 2. Extract Finalize Hook Fixture Writer
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/tests/required-hook-failure-policy.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** The finalize hook module source and file-writing setup are duplicated across finalize-cleanup tests.  
**Suggestion:** Add a `writeFinalizeHook(projectRoot, { className, body, policy = "required" })` helper that writes `.senti/plugins/fixture/hooks/finalize.js` and returns the matching snapshot metadata.

findings.title: 3. Remove Redundant Initial Plugin Lifecycle Value
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** `let pluginLifecycle = { warnings: [], issueLogEntries: [], data: {} };` is immediately overwritten before meaningful use in `runTeardownTransactionOwned`, so the initializer is dead state.  
**Suggestion:** Change it to `let pluginLifecycle;` or declare it at the assignment point after `postResult` succeeds.

findings.title: 4. Centralize Required Hook Failure Details
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R3  
**Issue:** Required hook failure message and metadata extraction are duplicated between `finalizeRequiredPluginHookFailure` and the teardown failure path.  
**Suggestion:** Add a small helper, for example `requiredHookFailureDetails(pluginLifecycle)`, returning `{ message, pluginId, hook }`, and use it in both places.

findings.title: 5. Avoid Reaching Into Envelope Internals For Post-Hook Errors
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** `new Error(postResult.env.errors[0].messages[0])` depends on the internal shape of `Envelope` errors at the call site.  
**Suggestion:** Have `runFinalizePostHooks` return the caught error alongside the envelope, e.g. `{ ok: false, env, error }`, so `failBeforeCommit(postResult.env, postResult.error)` does not need to inspect envelope internals.

findings.title: 1. Remove Redundant Catch Block
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`
**Requirement:** R7
**Issue:** `writeFlowState()` wraps the lifecycle execution in `try { ... } catch (error) { throw error; }`, which adds no behavior and makes the required-hook control flow harder to scan.
**Suggestion:** Remove the redundant `try/catch` and keep the lifecycle failure handling inline after `runFlowCommandWithPluginLifecycle()`.

findings.title: 2. Rename Callback to Match Its Side Effect
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`
**Requirement:** R6
**Issue:** `writeFlowState(extra, writePrepareFiles)` now receives a callback that writes spec/source files before creating flow state, but the name `writePrepareFiles` is broad and easy to confuse with `writeFlowState()` itself.
**Suggestion:** Rename the parameter to something more explicit, such as `writeSpecFilesBeforeState`, or extract a helper like `createPrepareFilesAndState(state, writeSpecFiles)` to make the “hooks first, files second” ordering obvious.

findings.title: 3. Avoid Revalidating The Full Hook Snapshot On Every Dispatch
findings.body:
**File:** `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`
**Requirement:** R1
**Issue:** `runFlowCommandHooks()` calls `validateHookSnapshot(snapshot)` every time hooks are dispatched. A lifecycle with pre and post hooks validates the same snapshot twice, and future callers may repeat this further.
**Suggestion:** Move snapshot validation to `runFlowCommandWithPluginLifecycle()` once per lifecycle, or introduce a small validated snapshot wrapper/helper so callers do not repeatedly scan the same data.

findings.title: 4. Make Outcome Kind Constants Shared
findings.body:
**File:** `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`
**Requirement:** R2
**Issue:** Outcome kind strings are repeated inline across `FlowCommandHookExecutionOutcome`, `runFlowCommandHooks()`, and `composePluginLifecycleResult()`. This increases typo risk as the typed outcome model grows.
**Suggestion:** Define constants or a frozen set for outcome kinds, similar to `FLOW_COMMAND_HOOK_FAILURE_POLICIES`, and use them consistently.

findings.title: 5. Simplify Lifecycle Failure Composition Naming
findings.body:
**File:** `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`
**Requirement:** R7
**Issue:** `pluginLifecycleFailure(failure, result, pre = null)` passes a hook result named `failure` into `composePluginLifecycleResult()` as `terminal`. The naming shifts between “failure” and “terminal”, which makes pre-failure vs post-failure behavior harder to follow.
**Suggestion:** Use one term consistently, for example `terminalHooks`, and inline `pluginLifecycleFailure()` if it remains a one-line wrapper.

findings.title: 6. Keep Envelope Validation Near Result Handling
findings.body:
**File:** `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`
**Requirement:** R3
**Issue:** `isEnvelopeLike()` was moved away from the other dispatch helpers and now sits between `loadHookClass()` and `runFlowCommandHooks()`. It is only used by hook execution.
**Suggestion:** Keep `isEnvelopeLike()` immediately before `runFlowCommandHooks()` with a short name like `isHookEnvelopeResult()`, making its scope and purpose clearer.

findings.title: 1. Extract repeated fake flow manager transition logic
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/set-step-impl-repair.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The inline `flowManager.updateStepStatus` implementations repeat the same transition-application loop in multiple tests. This makes later API changes easier to miss across fixtures.  
**Suggestion:** Introduce a small test helper such as `createFlowManagerStub(state, transitions)` or `applyTransitionChanges(state, transition)` and reuse it in both test cases.

findings.title: 2. Extract plugin fixture installation setup
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/finalize-cleanup-transaction-v2.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The plugin setup now writes the same config and hook source into both the main root and worktree, then manually stages and commits the worktree copy. This is dense fixture plumbing inside the test body and is likely to be repeated by future finalize plugin tests.  
**Suggestion:** Extract a helper like `installFinalizeHookPlugin({ root, worktreePath, pluginId, hookSource })` that writes both runtime copies, stages the worktree paths, and commits them.

findings.title: 3. Avoid force-removing expected fixture files without an assertion
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/set-step-impl-repair.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R2  
**Issue:** Changing `fs.rmSync(... )` to `{ force: true }` removes the signal that `impl-review.json` and `impl-triage.json` were actually created by the fixture before the test deletes them. If fixture setup regresses, the test will silently continue with a different precondition.  
**Suggestion:** Assert file existence before removal, or use a helper such as `removeExpectedFixtureFile(path)` that checks `existsSync` and then removes the file.

findings.title: 1. Normalize Gate Finding Schema Across Artifacts
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/draft-gate-source.json`
**Requirement:** R1
**Issue:** Multiple gate artifacts report the same structural problems: duplicated finding payloads across `evaluations` and `observations`, repeated rationale fields, inconsistent field naming, and missing/nullable requirement traceability. This suggests the artifacts are being generated from inconsistent or under-specified interfaces rather than isolated file mistakes.
**Suggestion:** Define one shared gate-finding schema for all `*-gate-source.json` artifacts: canonical finding data stored once, location/observation references separated, consistent camelCase names, and required `requirementId` values.

findings.title: 2. Consolidate Required Hook Failure Language Across Spec And Tests
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/spec.md`
**Requirement:** R6
**Issue:** Required/advisory hook behavior and finalize-cleanup atomicity are repeated across `issue.md`, `draft.json`, `spec.md`, and test descriptions. The same policy surface is described in several places with slightly different wording, creating drift risk between requirements, acceptance criteria, and implementation tests.
**Suggestion:** Introduce a single named lifecycle failure matrix or protected-surface list in the spec data, then reference it from rendered markdown, validation, scope, acceptance criteria, and tests.

findings.title: 3. Share Hook Fixture Builders Between Spec And Unit Tests
findings.body:
**File:** `specs/345-required-hook-failure-policy/tests/required-hook-failure-policy.test.js`
**Requirement:** R8
**Issue:** Hook snapshot/plugin fixture setup is duplicated in both spec-local tests and unit tests, including repeated hook metadata, config writing, hook source writing, and finalize plugin installation behavior. This creates parallel fixture conventions that can diverge as hook snapshot fields evolve.
**Suggestion:** Extract shared test helpers for hook snapshots and plugin installation, then use them from both spec tests and unit tests where feasible.

findings.title: 4. Align Hook Outcome Naming Across Plugin Registry And Callers
findings.body:
**File:** `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`
**Requirement:** R2
**Issue:** Outcome terms shift between `failure`, `terminal`, outcome kind strings, and lifecycle result composition, while callers such as finalize cleanup separately inspect failure details. The interface vocabulary is inconsistent across producer and consumer files.
**Suggestion:** Define shared outcome kind constants and use one term, such as `terminalHooks`, across `plugin-registry.js`, prepare, and finalize cleanup call sites.

findings.title: 5. Centralize Required Hook Failure Detail Extraction
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`
**Requirement:** R3
**Issue:** Required hook failure message/plugin/hook extraction is duplicated inside finalize cleanup, while prepare and plugin registry also participate in the same lifecycle failure model. This risks inconsistent user-facing failure messages between prepare and finalize paths.
**Suggestion:** Add a shared helper or lifecycle result method that exposes `{ message, pluginId, hook }` for terminal required-hook failures, and have prepare/finalize callers use that interface instead of rebuilding details locally.

blockingFindings.title: Required prepare hook failure leaves prepared flow state behind
blockingFindings.issue: `writeFlowState()` now runs `writePrepareFiles()`, creates `flow.json`, publishes the repair baseline, and creates the active flow inside the plugin lifecycle `main`. If a required `prepare.post` hook fails, `runFlowCommandWithPluginLifecycle()` returns `ok:false`, but the catch path only returns an envelope and does not roll back those already-written prepare artifacts or active flow state.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Make required `prepare.post` failure transactional in `writeFlowState()`: either run required post hooks before committing the flow state, or explicitly remove the newly written spec files/flow state, undo active-flow registration, and revert repair-baseline publication before returning `PLUGIN_HOOK_REQUIRED_FAILED`. Add a regression test for a required `prepare.post` failure that asserts no active flow/state/spec artifacts remain.
blockingFindings.rationale: R2 covers required hook failure handling for `run-prepare-spec.js`. A required hook failure is a blocking policy decision; leaving the flow prepared after reporting failure contradicts fail-stop semantics and can corrupt subsequent flow runs.

findings.title: Required prepare hook failure leaves prepared flow state behind
findings.body: `writeFlowState()` now runs `writePrepareFiles()`, creates `flow.json`, publishes the repair baseline, and creates the active flow inside the plugin lifecycle `main`. If a required `prepare.post` hook fails, `runFlowCommandWithPluginLifecycle()` returns `ok:false`, but the catch path only returns an envelope and does not roll back those already-written prepare artifacts or active flow state.
findings.rationale: R2 covers required hook failure handling for `run-prepare-spec.js`. A required hook failure is a blocking policy decision; leaving the flow prepared after reporting failure contradicts fail-stop semantics and can corrupt subsequent flow runs.

blockingFindings.title: Prepare pre hooks run before required spec artifacts exist
blockingFindings.issue: `writeFlowState()` now wraps both source-file creation and `flowManager.create()` inside `runFlowCommandWithPluginLifecycle()`. That means newly supported `prepare.pre` hooks execute before `spec.json`, `spec.md`, and optional `issue.md` are written, while hook execution still builds contexts with `requireSpecArtifacts: true`. A required prepare pre hook that needs the prepare artifacts will fail before the command has created the artifacts it is expected to validate or consume.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Create the prepare source files before invoking `prepare.pre`, then run the required pre hook, create `flow.json`, and keep the rollback path deleting the created files and plugin artifacts on required hook failure.
blockingFindings.rationale: R6 covers prepare hook behavior in `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`; the implementation contradicts the expected lifecycle ordering by enabling `prepare.pre` while withholding the artifacts required by the hook context.

blockingFindings.title: Required finalize post hook failure can occur after spec-only completion
blockingFindings.issue: In the spec-only branch, `runSpecOnlyCompletion()` is executed before `runFinalizePostHooks()`. If a required finalize post hook fails, the command returns `PLUGIN_HOOK_REQUIRED_FAILED` after active-flow cleanup/report side effects have already completed, with no rollback or recovery journal path protecting those changes.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Run spec-only completion through the same transactional lifecycle pattern as teardown, or add an explicit rollback/recovery step around `runSpecOnlyCompletion()` before returning a required post-hook failure.
blockingFindings.rationale: R7 maps to finalize cleanup behavior and required hook failures. A required post-hook failure is mandatory blocking behavior, but this branch reports failure after mutating flow state, leaving the command in a partially completed state.

findings.title: Prepare pre hooks run before required spec artifacts exist
findings.body: `writeFlowState()` now wraps both source-file creation and `flowManager.create()` inside `runFlowCommandWithPluginLifecycle()`. That means newly supported `prepare.pre` hooks execute before `spec.json`, `spec.md`, and optional `issue.md` are written, while hook execution still builds contexts with `requireSpecArtifacts: true`. A required prepare pre hook that needs the prepare artifacts will fail before the command has created the artifacts it is expected to validate or consume.
findings.rationale: R6 covers prepare hook behavior in `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`; the implementation contradicts the expected lifecycle ordering by enabling `prepare.pre` while withholding the artifacts required by the hook context.

findings.title: Required finalize post hook failure can occur after spec-only completion
findings.body: In the spec-only branch, `runSpecOnlyCompletion()` is executed before `runFinalizePostHooks()`. If a required finalize post hook fails, the command returns `PLUGIN_HOOK_REQUIRED_FAILED` after active-flow cleanup/report side effects have already completed, with no rollback or recovery journal path protecting those changes.
findings.rationale: R7 maps to finalize cleanup behavior and required hook failures. A required post-hook failure is mandatory blocking behavior, but this branch reports failure after mutating flow state, leaving the command in a partially completed state.

blockingFindings.title: Required finalize pre-hook failures can leave unrolled-back changes
blockingFindings.issue: `RunFinalizeCleanupCommand.execute()` now runs `runFinalizePreHooks()` before `runPersistedTeardownIfPresent()` and before `runTeardownTransactionOwned()` establishes its rollback/recovery handling. If a required `finalize-cleanup.pre` hook writes outside `plugin-artifacts` and then fails, the command returns `PLUGIN_HOOK_REQUIRED_FAILED` after only removing plugin artifacts, leaving other hook side effects in the repo/worktree.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Run finalize pre-hooks inside the existing teardown transaction after the pre-commit snapshots/recovery journal are prepared, or wrap the early pre-hook path in equivalent rollback coverage. In `RunFinalizeCleanupCommand.execute()`, avoid returning directly from the early `runFinalizePreHooks()` path unless all hook side effects are covered by the same restoration logic used by `runTeardownTransactionOwned()`.
blockingFindings.rationale: R7 covers finalize cleanup required-hook failure behavior for `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`. A required hook failure is a blocking policy condition, and leaving repository mutations behind violates the fail-stop/restore guardrail for cleanup failures.

findings.title: Required finalize pre-hook failures can leave unrolled-back changes
findings.body: `RunFinalizeCleanupCommand.execute()` now runs `runFinalizePreHooks()` before `runPersistedTeardownIfPresent()` and before `runTeardownTransactionOwned()` establishes its rollback/recovery handling. If a required `finalize-cleanup.pre` hook writes outside `plugin-artifacts` and then fails, the command returns `PLUGIN_HOOK_REQUIRED_FAILED` after only removing plugin artifacts, leaving other hook side effects in the repo/worktree.
findings.rationale: R7 covers finalize cleanup required-hook failure behavior for `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`. A required hook failure is a blocking policy condition, and leaving repository mutations behind violates the fail-stop/restore guardrail for cleanup failures.

nonBlockingImprovements.title: 1. Consolidate review exclusion inputs
nonBlockingImprovements.issue:
**File:** `src/flow/commands/review.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `resolveReviewTarget` now accepts both `excludeMatcher` and `exclusions`, which represent the same policy in two forms. This creates a drift risk if callers pass a matcher built from one exclusion list and a different raw list to `collectCommittedAndStagedDiff`.  
**Suggestion:** Pass a single exclusion policy object, e.g. `{ matcher, paths }`, or construct both inside `resolveReviewTarget` from one `exclusions` argument.

**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `resolveReviewTarget` now accepts both `excludeMatcher` and `exclusions`, which represent the same policy in two forms. This creates a drift risk if callers pass a matcher built from one exclusion list and a different raw list to `collectCommittedAndStagedDiff`.  
**Suggestion:** Pass a single exclusion policy object, e.g. `{ matcher, paths }`, or construct both inside `resolveReviewTarget` from one `exclusions` argument.

nonBlockingImprovements.title: 2. Avoid post-construction identity mutation
nonBlockingImprovements.issue:
**File:** `src/flow/commands/review.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `applyImplReviewDispositionPolicy` mutates `typed.findingId` and `typed.fingerprint` after `finding.withDisposition(...)`. That weakens the class/object invariant: a finding can temporarily exist with stale identity, and callers must remember to patch it afterward.  
**Suggestion:** Move identity preservation into the construction path, either by making `withDisposition(disposition, requirementIds, fingerprint)` preserve/override identity, or by adding a dedicated method such as `withDispositionAndIdentity(...)`.

nonBlockingImprovements.issue:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** The same `finalizeCleanupPrePluginLifecycleContext` + `runFinalizePreHooks` + early return pattern appears in both lifecycle branches and again in `runTeardownTransactionOwned`. This makes required-hook stop behavior easier to accidentally diverge.  
**Suggestion:** Add a helper such as `runFinalizeCleanupPreLifecycle(ctx, state, { worktreePath, mainRepoPath, specId })` that returns `{ ok, env, pluginContext, pluginPre }`, and reuse it in all three call sites.

nonBlockingImprovements.title: 2. Reuse Required Hook Failure Envelope Helper
nonBlockingImprovements.issue:

**File:** `src/flow/commands/review.js`  
**Requirement:** R8

**Suggestion:** Pass a single exclusion policy object, e.g. `{ matcher, paths }`, or construct both inside `resolveReviewTarget` from one `exclusions` argument.

findings.title: 2. Avoid post-construction identity mutation
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/commands/review.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `applyImplReviewDispositionPolicy` mutates `typed.findingId` and `typed.fingerprint` after `finding.withDisposition(...)`. That weakens the class/object invariant: a finding can temporarily exist with stale identity, and callers must remember to patch it afterward.  
**Suggestion:** Move identity preservation into the construction path, either by making `withDisposition(disposition, requirementIds, fingerprint)` preserve/override identity, or by adding a dedicated method such as `withDispositionAndIdentity(...)`.

**Issue:** `runFinalizePostHooks` passes `{ command: "finalize-cleanup", hook: "post", flow: pluginContext.flow, result }` on one line, while the pre-hook call uses the multi-line shape. This is a minor consistency issue, but this code now encodes the structured runner contract and should stay easy to scan.  
**Suggestion:** Format the post-hook options object like the pre-hook object, or extract a small `finalizeHookRequest(pluginContext, hook, result)` helper used by both pre and post calls.

findings.title: 1. Narrow the Legacy Artifact Exception
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-gate.js`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** The new `catch` suppresses any constructor error for non-latest artifacts with `blockingFindings.length === 0`. That can hide unrelated malformed artifact data, because the code does not verify that the failure is specifically the expected historical “missing stable finding identities” case.  
**Suggestion:** Add a small predicate or explicit error check for the known legacy condition, then continue only for that case. Otherwise rethrow. This keeps the compatibility path narrow and makes future artifact validation failures visible.

findings.title: 1. Remove no-op try/catch around lifecycle writes
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** `writeFlowState()` wraps the hook snapshot, file creation, lifecycle execution, and repair publication in `try { ... } catch (error) { throw error; }`, which adds no behavior and makes the new control flow harder to read.  
**Suggestion:** Remove the `try/catch` and let errors propagate directly. Keep the required-hook rollback branch inline after `runFlowCommandWithPluginLifecycle()`.

findings.title: 2. Rename `writePrepareFiles` to clarify side effects and return value
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** The new `writeFlowState(extra, writePrepareFiles)` parameter name is vague: the callback both creates missing prepare source files and returns the subset it created for rollback. That return contract is important for required hook failure behavior.  
**Suggestion:** Rename the parameter to something like `createMissingPrepareSourceFiles` or `writePrepareFilesAndReturnCreatedPaths`, and consider renaming `createdSourceFiles` to `createdPrepareFiles` for consistency with `writeSpecFiles()`.

findings.title: 3. Avoid rollback deleting pre-existing plugin artifacts
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** `rollbackRequiredPrepareHookFailure()` always removes `plugin-artifacts` recursively, but the helper only tracks newly created source files. If `plugin-artifacts` existed before this prepare attempt, a required pre-hook failure could delete pre-existing content, which exceeds rollback of this command’s changes.  
**Suggestion:** Track whether `plugin-artifacts` existed before lifecycle execution, or track created artifact paths if available. Only remove the directory when it was created by this prepare attempt.

findings.title: 4. Use non-deprecated directory removal API
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** `fs.rmdirSync(specDir)` is used after checking the directory is empty. In modern Node.js code, `fs.rmSync(..., { dir options })` is generally preferred and is already used in the same helper.  
**Suggestion:** Replace `fs.rmdirSync(specDir)` with `fs.rmSync(specDir, { recursive: false, force: true })` or the project’s existing preferred empty-directory removal helper if one exists in this file.

findings.title: 1. Centralize Outcome Kind Constants
findings.body:
**File:** `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`  
**Requirement:** R2  
**Issue:** Outcome kind strings (`"success"`, `"business-failure"`, `"integrity-failure"`) are repeated across validation, construction, and result composition. This makes future changes error-prone.  
**Suggestion:** Define a frozen `FLOW_COMMAND_HOOK_OUTCOME_KINDS` object or static factory methods on `FlowCommandHookExecutionOutcome` such as `success()`, `businessFailure(policy, failure)`, and `integrityFailure(failure)`.

findings.title: 2. Avoid Revalidating Entire Hook Snapshot Per Dispatch
findings.body:
**File:** `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** `runFlowCommandHooks()` validates every snapshot entry on each invocation, even when only one `command`/`hook` subset will run. Lifecycle execution calls this twice, duplicating validation work.  
**Suggestion:** Validate the snapshot once at the lifecycle boundary, or filter matching plans first and validate only the plans about to execute. Keep hard rejection before execution, but avoid repeated full-snapshot scans.

findings.title: 3. Preserve Multiple Advisory Failure Outcomes
findings.body:
**File:** `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`  
**Requirement:** R2  
**Issue:** `outcome` is overwritten on each advisory business failure, so if multiple advisory hooks fail, only the last failure is represented in the typed outcome while earlier failures only remain in warnings.  
**Suggestion:** Either make `FlowCommandHookExecutionOutcome.failure` hold an array for business failures, or keep a separate `failures` collection and construct the outcome from all advisory failures at the end.

findings.title: 4. Rename `terminal` for Lifecycle Composition Clarity
findings.body:
**File:** `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** In `composePluginLifecycleResult(result, pre, terminal, ok)`, `terminal` actually means either the post-hook result or the failing hook result. The name hides lifecycle semantics and makes the outcome selection harder to read.  
**Suggestion:** Rename it to `hookResult` or `finalHookResult`, and consider passing an options object to make pre/post/failure roles explicit.

findings.title: 1. Remove redundant fixture directory creation
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/commands/review.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The new test creates `specs/demo` before `initTestRepo(...)`, then creates the same directory again immediately after reading `baseSha`. Since `initTestRepo` already receives `specs/demo/flow.json`, the first explicit `fs.mkdirSync(...)` appears redundant, and the second one is enough before writing `spec.json`.  
**Suggestion:** Delete the first `fs.mkdirSync(join(tmp, "specs/demo"), { recursive: true });` in `"applies configured exclusions to the fallback tracked diff"` to keep the fixture setup tighter.

findings.title: 1. Extract repeated plugin hook registration setup
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/finalize-cleanup-transaction-v2.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** The test now duplicates plugin runtime setup across main/worktree paths: config writing, hook source writing, state hook metadata, and matching `failurePolicy` values. This makes future changes to hook metadata easy to miss in one place.  
**Suggestion:** Add a small local helper in this test file, such as `installFinalizeHookPlugin({ root, worktreePath, pluginId, hook, failurePolicy, source })`, that writes both configs/hooks and returns the `flowCommandHooks` entry.

findings.title: 2. Avoid string duplication for failure policy literals
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/finalize-cleanup-transaction-v2.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** The same `failurePolicy` value is repeated in both hook class definitions and serialized fixture state. If they diverge, the test may stop asserting the intended behavior.  
**Suggestion:** Define a local constant per test, for example `const failurePolicy = "advisory";`, and interpolate/use it in both the hook source and `fixture.state.plugins` entry.

findings.title: 3. Rename `stopped` to describe the result
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/finalize-cleanup-transaction-v2.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `stopped` describes an expected state rather than the value returned by `runFinalize`, which slightly obscures the assertion flow.  
**Suggestion:** Rename it to `result` or `finalizeResult` and keep the failure expectation in the assertions.

findings.title: 1. Reuse the stale finding identity value
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/finding-gate-readiness.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The test duplicates `"0".repeat(64)` for both `findingId` and `fingerprint`, which makes the intended “same stale identity” relationship implicit.  
**Suggestion:** Introduce a local constant, e.g. `const staleFindingIdentity = "0".repeat(64);`, and assign it to both fields. This improves readability and avoids accidental divergence if the value changes later.

findings.title: 1. Extract repeated mock transition application
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/set-step-impl-repair.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The mocked `updateStepStatus` implementation repeats the same transition-change application logic in multiple test cases. This makes future API changes or status mutation behavior easy to update inconsistently.  
**Suggestion:** Extract a local helper such as `applyStepTransition(state, transition)` or `createFlowManager(state, transitions)` and reuse it across these tests.

findings.title: 2. Avoid silent fixture cleanup with `force: true`
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/set-step-impl-repair.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R2  
**Issue:** Changing `fs.rmSync(... )` to `fs.rmSync(..., { force: true })` hides cases where the expected fixture files were never created. In a unit test, that can mask setup drift and reduce the test’s diagnostic value.  
**Suggestion:** If the files are expected to exist, keep the strict removal. If absence is valid for this scenario, add an explicit comment or assertion around that condition so the intent is clear.

findings.title: 1. Centralize Required Hook Failure Handling
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R3  
**Issue:** Required hook failure envelopes and rollback/stop behavior are being introduced in multiple lifecycle paths, while `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js` has its own rollback handling for required prepare hook failures. This creates a cross-file risk that prepare and finalize commands report or clean up required hook failures differently.
**Suggestion:** Extract a shared lifecycle failure helper near the plugin lifecycle utilities, covering message, metadata shape, and required/advisory policy handling. Let prepare/finalize command files supply only command-specific rollback inputs.

findings.title: 2. Align Hook Lifecycle Naming Across Files
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** New names such as `finalizeCleanupPrePluginLifecycleContext`, `terminal`, `stopped`, and `writePrepareFiles` describe similar lifecycle concepts at different abstraction levels, but use inconsistent terms across `run-finalize-cleanup.js`, `run-prepare-spec.js`, `plugin-registry.js`, and tests.
**Suggestion:** Standardize vocabulary around `preHook`, `postHook`, `hookResult`, `lifecycleResult`, and `createdPaths`. Rename local variables and helpers to reflect those roles consistently.

findings.title: 3. Share Flow Command Hook Outcome Constants
findings.body:
**File:** `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`  
**Requirement:** R2  
**Issue:** Hook outcome and failure policy literals are repeated in production code and tests, especially `"success"`, `"business-failure"`, `"integrity-failure"`, `"required"`, and `"advisory"`. This increases the chance that tests and runtime behavior drift independently.
**Suggestion:** Define canonical constants or factory methods in the plugin registry module and reuse them in lifecycle code and tests where practical.

findings.title: 4. Consolidate Test Plugin Hook Fixture Setup
findings.body:
**File:** `tests/unit/flow/finalize-cleanup-transaction-v2.test.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** Multiple tests now hand-build plugin hook config, hook source files, serialized hook metadata, and failure policy values. Similar setup appears likely to spread across prepare/finalize lifecycle tests as required-hook behavior expands.
**Suggestion:** Add a shared test helper for installing flow command hook fixtures, including config, hook source, metadata entry, and failure policy. Use it across lifecycle-related unit tests.

nonBlockingImprovements.title: 1. Consolidate review exclusion inputs
nonBlockingImprovements.issue:
**File:** `src/flow/commands/review.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `resolveReviewTarget` now accepts both `excludeMatcher` and `exclusions`, which represent the same policy in two forms. This creates a drift risk if callers pass a matcher built from one exclusion list and a different raw list to `collectCommittedAndStagedDiff`.  
**Suggestion:** Pass a single exclusion policy object, e.g. `{ matcher, paths }`, or construct both inside `resolveReviewTarget` from one `exclusions` argument.

nonBlockingImprovements.title: 2. Avoid post-construction identity mutation

findings.title: 1. Consolidate review exclusion inputs
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/commands/review.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `resolveReviewTarget` now accepts both `excludeMatcher` and `exclusions`, which represent the same policy in two forms. This creates a drift risk if callers pass a matcher built from one exclusion list and a different raw list to `collectCommittedAndStagedDiff`.  
**Suggestion:** Pass a single exclusion policy object, e.g. `{ matcher, paths }`, or construct both inside `resolveReviewTarget` from one `exclusions` argument.

findings.title: 2. Avoid post-construction identity mutation
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/commands/review.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `applyImplReviewDispositionPolicy` mutates `typed.findingId` and `typed.fingerprint` after `finding.withDisposition(...)`. That weakens the class/object invariant: a finding can temporarily exist with stale identity, and callers must remember to patch it afterward.  
**Suggestion:** Move identity preservation into the construction path, either by making `withDisposition(disposition, requirementIds, fingerprint)` preserve/override identity, or by adding a dedicated method such as `withDispositionAndIdentity(...)`.

findings.title: 1. Extract Repeated Pre-Hook Setup
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** The same `finalizeCleanupPrePluginLifecycleContext` + `runFinalizePreHooks` + early return pattern appears in both lifecycle branches and again in `runTeardownTransactionOwned`. This makes required-hook stop behavior easier to accidentally diverge.  
**Suggestion:** Add a helper such as `runFinalizeCleanupPreLifecycle(ctx, state, { worktreePath, mainRepoPath, specId })` that returns `{ ok, env, pluginContext, pluginPre }`, and reuse it in all three call sites.

findings.title: 2. Reuse Required Hook Failure Envelope Helper
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R3  
**Issue:** `finalizeRequiredPluginHookFailure(pluginLifecycle)` exists, but `runTeardownTransactionOwned` rebuilds a near-duplicate `Envelope.fail(...)` for required post-hook failures. The duplicated construction already differs in metadata shape and message assembly.  
**Suggestion:** Extend `finalizeRequiredPluginHookFailure` to accept optional extra metadata, or create one shared helper for required plugin hook failures, then wrap it with `failBeforeCommit(...)` in the transaction path.

findings.title: 3. Clarify Pre-Hook Context Naming
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** `finalizeCleanupPrePluginLifecycleContext` reads like a lifecycle context for all finalize cleanup plugin work, but it actually selects a pre-hook-specific artifact authority and may discard artifacts on success. That distinction is central to preventing teardown side effects after required pre-hook failure.  
**Suggestion:** Rename it to something more explicit, for example `finalizeCleanupPreHookContext` or `finalizeCleanupPreHookArtifactContext`, and keep `finalizeCleanupPluginLifecycleContext` for the normal post/retained artifact context.

findings.title: 4. Avoid Inline Compact Hook Invocation Object
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js`  
**Requirement:** R4  
**Issue:** `runFinalizePostHooks` passes `{ command: "finalize-cleanup", hook: "post", flow: pluginContext.flow, result }` on one line, while the pre-hook call uses the multi-line shape. This is a minor consistency issue, but this code now encodes the structured runner contract and should stay easy to scan.  
**Suggestion:** Format the post-hook options object like the pre-hook object, or extract a small `finalizeHookRequest(pluginContext, hook, result)` helper used by both pre and post calls.

findings.title: 1. Bound JSON Candidate Scanning
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-gate.js`  
**Requirement:** R8  
**Issue:** `extractJsonCandidate()` scans the entire provider output with no explicit size bound. This violates the bounded-resource-usage guardrail for bulk/recursive-style processing over external text.  
**Suggestion:** Add a maximum candidate input length or scan limit before the brace-balancing loop, using an existing project constant if available or a local `MAX_JSON_CANDIDATE_SCAN_CHARS`.

findings.title: 2. Rename Parser State Flags
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-gate.js`  
**Requirement:** R1  
**Issue:** The brace parser uses `quoted` and `escaped`, which are correct but slightly ambiguous. `quoted` can read like “this character is quoted” rather than “the parser is currently inside a string.”  
**Suggestion:** Rename `quoted` to `inString` and `escaped` to `escapeNext` to make the state machine easier to audit.

findings.title: 3. Extract Historical Advisory Predicate
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-gate.js`  
**Requirement:** R4  
**Issue:** The catch block embeds a domain rule inline: non-latest artifacts with zero `blockingFindings` are ignored because historical advisory-only reports do not create obligations. This makes the exception path harder to distinguish from generic constructor failure handling.  
**Suggestion:** Extract the condition into a small helper such as `isHistoricalAdvisoryOnlyArtifact(candidate, raw)` and use it in the catch block. This keeps the policy named and easier to test or adjust later.

findings.title: 1. Remove no-op try/catch around lifecycle writes
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`  
**Requirement:** R7  
**Issue:** `writeFlowState()` wraps the hook snapshot, file creation, lifecycle execution, and repair publication in `try { ... } catch (error) { throw error; }`, which adds no behavior and makes the new control flow harder to read.  
**Suggestion:** Remove the `try/catch` and let errors propagate directly. Keep the required-hook rollback branch inline after `runFlowCommandWithPluginLifecycle()`.

findings.title: 2. Rename `writePrepareFiles` to clarify side effects and return value
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** The new `writeFlowState(extra, writePrepareFiles)` parameter name is vague: the callback both creates missing prepare source files and returns the subset it created for rollback. That return contract is important for required hook failure behavior.  
**Suggestion:** Rename the parameter to something like `createMissingPrepareSourceFiles` or `writePrepareFilesAndReturnCreatedPaths`, and consider renaming `createdSourceFiles` to `createdPrepareFiles` for consistency with `writeSpecFiles()`.

findings.title: 3. Avoid rollback deleting pre-existing plugin artifacts
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** `rollbackRequiredPrepareHookFailure()` always removes `plugin-artifacts` recursively, but the helper only tracks newly created source files. If `plugin-artifacts` existed before this prepare attempt, a required pre-hook failure could delete pre-existing content, which exceeds rollback of this command’s changes.  
**Suggestion:** Track whether `plugin-artifacts` existed before lifecycle execution, or track created artifact paths if available. Only remove the directory when it was created by this prepare attempt.

findings.title: 4. Use non-deprecated directory removal API
findings.body:
**File:** `src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js`  
**Requirement:** R6  
**Issue:** `fs.rmdirSync(specDir)` is used after checking the directory is empty. In modern Node.js code, `fs.rmSync(..., { dir options })` is generally preferred and is already used in the same helper.  
**Suggestion:** Replace `fs.rmdirSync(specDir)` with `fs.rmSync(specDir, { recursive: false, force: true })` or the project’s existing preferred empty-directory removal helper if one exists in this file.

findings.title: 1. Centralize Outcome Kind Constants

**File:** `src/lib/plugin-registry.js`  
**Requirement:** R2  
**Issue:** Outcome kind strings (`"success"`, `"business-failure"`, `"integrity-failure"`) are repeated across validation, construction, and result composition. This makes future changes error-prone.  
**Suggestion:** Define a frozen `FLOW_COMMAND_HOOK_OUTCOME_KINDS` object or static factory methods on `FlowCommandHookExecutionOutcome` such as `success()`, `businessFailure(policy, failure)`, and `integrityFailure(failure)`.
